requirements.requirement: The repaired supervisor starts the requested number of short jobs, reaps every child, and records even jobs with exit status 0 and odd jobs with exit status 3.
requirements.summary: A live six-job run directly showed six child processes while the supervisor was running, then six correctly classified result rows and zero system-wide zombies after completion. Separate 8-job and post-restart 10-job runs also produced exactly the requested number of correct rows.

requirements.requirement: Previous results are preserved while new job results are recorded.
requirements.summary: The original header and previous,0,0 row remained present while successive runs appended the expected number of new records. They also persisted across the node restart.

requirements.requirement: The supervisor remains available until its children have finished.
requirements.summary: During a bounded six-job run, the supervisor was alive concurrently with all six children. It exited successfully only after the children completed and their six results had been appended.

requirements.requirement: The installed operating-system release and kernel are preserved, using software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: Before and after implementation and restart, the node remained AlmaLinux 9.6 on kernel 5.14.0-570.12.1.el9_6.x86_64. The repaired script compiled and ran with the already-installed Python 3.9 runtime.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral evidence. The supervisor launches the requested children, stays alive while they run, reaps them, appends correct parity-based statuses without losing prior data, and continues working after the mandatory node restart. The platform was preserved. Operational hygiene is strong apart from an apparently retained backup file.
limitations: No final inventory of /srv/legacy2/child-process-reaping was captured, so the complete final set of auxiliary files is not directly established. In particular, repeated py_compile checks may have created a persistent __pycache__ directory, but the evidence neither confirms nor disproves its final presence.
The retained supervisor.py.bak is inferred from its successful creation and the absence of any removal in the complete command timeline; a direct final directory listing was not captured.
Requirement R2 cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: The source replacement, bounded validation runs, result appends, and reboot all had clear task-verification or mandatory restart-protocol roles. The failed /usr/bin/python attempt stopped before its copy or overwrite operations, so no mutation is evidenced from that attempt. One unnecessary retained artifact is evident: supervisor.py.bak was created during installation and no later command removed it; this is low-risk but abandoned residue. The restart protocol itself was complete: healthy pre-restart state and boot ID, acknowledgement, a changed post-restart boot ID, persisted data/source, successful recovered workload behavior, zero zombies, and no failed units. Lifecycle snapshots show no new failed services, listening exposure, or package damage.
